newsitem.title: ITALY: Lira ERM negotiations to start very shortly-Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Lira ERM negotiations to start very shortly-Prodi.

text.p: The Italian government plans to open negotiations for the lira re-entry to the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) shortly, Prime Minister Romano Prodi said minutes after the lower house of parliament approved the budget.
"From today, tomorrow or the day after we will start negotiations for the lira's return to the ERM," Prodi told reporters.

The 1997 austerity budget, which is designed to tear 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) off next year's projected public sector deficit, was given the green light in the turbulent lower house after a month of controversy and debate.
The package now passes to the upper house (Senate), which is firmly controlled by the centre-left government and has until Christmas to ratify the measures.
The lira crashed out of the ERM during a currency crisis in 1992.

Prodi has repeatedly said he wants the lira to return to the ERM fold before the end of the year. Most analysts expect the lira back in the currency grid in time for the European Union's Dublin summit on December 13-14.
